statistical_scope_note: All reported pairwise differences and metric values represent validation sample point estimates, not proof of statistically significant superiority or inferiority.

pr_auc_point_estimate_drops.finding: In these validation experiments, each model family exhibited lower PR-AUC point estimates when trained with heavy inverse-class weights.

evidence.logistic_regression: -21.0% relative PR-AUC drop in point estimate (0.1755 -> 0.1387)
evidence.random_forest: -14.6% relative PR-AUC drop in point estimate (0.2810 -> 0.2399)
evidence.xgboost: -24.0% relative PR-AUC drop in point estimate (0.2909 -> 0.2212)

recall_gain_divergence.logistic_regression: Gained nominal recall at 0.50 (0.0% -> 50.0%, +21 TP observations) due to intercept shift upward, but generated 185 false alarms (precision 10.19%).
recall_gain_divergence.xgboost: Gained modest recall at 0.50 (28.57% -> 35.71%, +3 TP observations), while false alarms increased from 18 to 30.
recall_gain_divergence.random_forest: Observed lower recall at 0.50 (11.90% -> 4.76%, -3 TP observations, dropping from 5 to 2). A plausible contributing factor is that unconstrained tree depth in a 346-feature space containing 293 sparse dummy columns from date_of_birth may have led weighted trees to isolate positive training noise on sparse splits, reducing generalization. However, definitive attribution requires controlled ablation.

brier_score_observations.finding: In these experiments, class-balanced variants exhibited higher (worse) Brier scores than their unweighted counterparts. Brier score reflects overall mean squared error relative to the low base rate (3.67%), which was worsened by score inflation under balanced loss. However, formal clinical calibration across risk deciles (slope, intercept, reliability curves) has not been assessed.

threshold_tuning_vs_class_weighting.finding: Current validation evidence favors investigating decision threshold adjustment for existing unweighted models rather than training heavily class-weighted variants. Operating comparisons derived strictly from Task 3.1 validation sweep data (with zero test-set access) demonstrate that adjusting the unweighted model cutoff achieves competitive or higher sensitivity with fewer false alarms than the balanced models at threshold 0.50.
validation_point_estimate_evidence: Standard XGBoost at validation cutoff T=0.20 achieves Recall 40.48% (17 TP) and Precision 34.00% (33 FP, PR-AUC 0.2909), compared to Balanced XGBoost at 0.50 (Recall 35.71%, Precision 33.33%, PR-AUC 0.2212).

Standard XGBoost at validation cutoff T=0.13 achieves Recall 47.62% (20 TP) and Precision 32.79% (41 FP, PR-AUC 0.2909), catching 5 more true cases than Balanced XGBoost with a higher validation F1 (0.3883 vs 0.3448).

Standard Logistic Regression at validation cutoff T≈0.1036 matches 50% recall with 127 FP (Precision 14.19%, F1 0.2211), compared to Balanced Logistic Regression at 0.50 which produces 185 FP (Precision 10.19%, F1 0.1694).

proposed_future_weighting_experiments.strategy: Moderate / Sub-Linear Class Weighting (w1 = sqrt(N0 / N1) ≈ 4.72)
proposed_future_weighting_experiments.hypothesis: Test whether a milder square-root weighting factor offers a better empirical trade-off between minority sensitivity and ranking quality than full inverse weighting (w1 ≈ 22.3).
proposed_future_weighting_experiments.scientific_disclaimer: Untested research hypothesis only. There is no guarantee that moderate weighting will yield fewer false alerts or higher PR-AUC than the unweighted baseline.
proposed_future_weighting_experiments.execution_status: Proposed concept only; strictly not executed in Task 3.2.

proposed_future_weighting_experiments.hypothesis: Test whether dynamically down-weighting easy, well-classified examples focuses gradient updates more effectively on borderline trajectories than scalar class multipliers.
proposed_future_weighting_experiments.scientific_disclaimer: Untested research hypothesis only. There is no guarantee that focal loss will achieve superior calibration or higher PR-AUC on this cohort.

limitations.provenance: Unresolved mixture of real clinic records (approx 400 children) and synthetic records (approx 100 children).
limitations.interval_censoring: 46 validation observation rows have zero recorded visits within (0, 180] days and are labeled negative under the heuristic.
limitations.child_clustering: 75 children across 1,143 visits; longitudinal clustering affects variance.
limitations.feature_disparity: Tabular models receive 346 features with 293 date_of_birth dummy columns and static perinatal factors; sequence models receive 20 timesteps of 49 dynamic features without static birth factors.
